proof:
On all strip thresholds $t$ from $u\cdot y-hg$ to $u\cdot y$, the own cap isolates the same triangle vertex, with area $V(2-t)^2/(9-s^2)$. Differentiating and averaging over the strip gives $k_u$ as stated in the vertex-value scale. Normalizing $u$ by $g$ multiplies scalar coarea by $g$, so their product is $k_u u$. All outside strips have zero coarea by the active-family theorem. The bounds $|s|<1/4,\ |u\cdot y|\le4\delta,\ g<2$ and the stated $\delta,h$ give the strict interval for $k_u$.

For a cone, evaluate the balance at its maximizing vertex. The dot product there is $2$ in that cone and at least $-5/4$ elsewhere. If $q$ is its total response menu weight, this gives $(19/5)q\le(21/8)(1-q)$, i.e. $q\le105/257$. Every balance requires all three cones, and Carathéodory in the plane gives three atoms for a minimal positive circuit. No two of the cones can balance, so the circuit has rank two.

A generic nonzero pure-base direction takes exactly one strict-side endpoint, with mass $v$; this is the saturation baseline, excluding the own base. The active-family theorem gives the indicated deficits. For a probability menu with $\sum_i\theta_i u_i/\Gamma(u_i)=0$, first reweight by $1/\Gamma(u_i)$ and renormalize to obtain balance of the vertex-value representatives. Testing at $A$ shows that the new combined weight in $B,C$ is at least $8/13$. Each representative has $\Gamma(U_j(s))=\sqrt{t_\sigma/2}\sqrt{1+s^2/3}$, so the ratio of maximum to minimum possible norm is at most $\sqrt{49/48}$. Returning to $\theta$ gives at least $(8/13)\sqrt{48/49}$ weight in $B,C$, as required.
statement:
For the actual three-triangle family and width range above, let $u$ be an active continuous normal scaled to maximum vertex value $2$ with other values $-1\pm s$, and let $g=\Gamma(u)$. In covariance-unit normalization its coarea response vector is $k_u u$ where
$$
k_u=\frac{9(2-u\cdot y+hg/2)}{9-s^2},\qquad 19/10<k_u<21/10.
$$
Each cone has total weight at most $105/257<4/9$ in every probability menu that balances these response vectors, hence so does every individual atom. Every minimal positive circuit has rank two and three atoms. The pure-base saturation baseline at zero is $v$, and the outside saturation deficits are zero in $A$, $v$ in $B,C$. Every probability menu balancing the covariance-unit continuous normals has weighted deficit at least $(8/13)\sqrt{48/49}\,v>v/2$.
title: The three-cone active family has uniformly small response atoms and positive saturation deficit
